description: environments whose labels name a numbered EQUATION — the class \eqref addresses, and the branch that renders '(3)' rather than a type word

sectioning commands whose titles are brace-matched so a title containing macros (\subsection{... \cref{thm:x}}) is not truncated; a label inside the title or following it across whitespace NAMES that section

Coarse class for a numbered object's DISPLAY name, carried alongside kind in the subject index. Not all indexed objects are the same sort of thing: a consumer asking what a paper CLAIMS wants assertions, one building on it wants constructions, and remarks/examples are neither. Keyed on display name rather than environment name because that is what the reader sees and what the converter emits. An unlisted kind gets an empty class — unclassified is honest, guessing is not.

environments that never NAME a labelled object — structural wrappers (\begin{document} encloses the whole file and would otherwise win every innermost match) and presentation containers that sit INSIDE the thing being labelled (\begin{figure}\begin{tabular}...\label{}). Resolution walks outward through these to the nearest environment that carries meaning; anything not listed keeps its own name, so a paper's custom result environment stays a node
